① OBSERVED (designer's friction log #25): "reflow2 cannot count its own derived relations. There is no tool to evaluate or materialise the 23 declared derived relations over a design, so the derived-to-asserted ratio needed a hand-written ~150-line script over the export." The owner agent needed the ratio to size storage for kept derived facts (test 4). NOT affected: each relation is still computed inside the tool that needs it (arrival_delta, closure_report, budget_report, detect_gaps …).

② PRECEDENT, searched in reflow2 and flo2: req:reflow2s-code-reasons-from-the-declared-meanings-and-every-derived-relationship-is-a-declared-rule (test 3, proposed 2026-09-28), which says derived relations MUST be declared rules; req:reflow2-keeps-the-knowledge-it-derives (test 4, proposed, baseline "0 of 23 derived results are kept"); req:derived-relations-and-reports-are-maintained-incrementally and cap:declared-rules-run-by-an-embedded-datalog-engine-and-updated-by-delta (planned). The 2026-09-22 export lesson in the hub trial log ("a client that re-implements reflow2's computations over the export file will drift from reflow2's own semantics, quietly") is the same risk this script now carries. Nothing in flo2's design.

③ CANDIDATES: (a) a served evaluator is missing, while the declarations exist in reflow2; (b) there is nothing to evaluate, because reflow2 declares no derived relation, only computes them; (c) the observation is wrong: some served report already returns these counts; (d) not in the component suspected — the "23 declared derived relations" the reporter named are the primitives study's declarations, not reflow2's.

⑤ MEASURED: `grep` over reflow2/schema/*.yaml for any derived, derivation, computed or rule section finds none. Each entry of primitives/analysis/classified/reflow2/derived.jsonl cites a source location, e.g. report.rs:1368 (delivered), detect.rs:3665 (realized), verify.rs:155 (checked), maturity.rs:299-343 (seams and couplings), claims.rs, budget.rs, closure.rs, temporal.rs:1047 (arrival delta), across about 15 core files. The declaration exists only there, hand-kept in another repo against line numbers. No served read returns the counts together: they are spread across separate reports with different shapes, and the impact closure is never materialised. ⇒ (b) and (d) HOLD, (c) is refuted, and (a) is the reporter's reading of a symptom.
The script re-derives 22 of the 23 formulas outside the server (the 23rd needs the gap detector's output), which is exactly the drift risk named in 2026-09-22's lesson.

⑥ CLASS: a set of relations that code relies on is maintained by hand in the code itself, with no declaration anything could check or run. It is test 3 of dec:what-a-true-knowledge-graph-is, unmet, and this is its first field symptom. Would declaring them have prevented this report? Yes. A declared rule set is what an evaluator, a count and the incremental engine would all read.

⑦/⑧ OWED, NOT DONE: nothing to pin yet. The fix is the proposed test-3 requirement itself. A pinning test is owed when its first declared rule lands: every derived relation the core computes appears in the served declaration, checked against the core's call sites.

⑨ NOT ESTABLISHED: whether each of the 22 formulas in the script matches the core's current semantics. The script was read, not diffed against the code.
